Xsuq_3Bh1e4.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 28: Eighth Night of Tahajjud
Xsuq_3Bh1e4.one_line: Night and day as signs calling for remembrance and gratitude, spending before the Day, and the man who slept a hundred years.
Xsuq_3Bh1e4.summary: Both reminders draw on verses recited in the rakaat just before them. The first takes the verse of Al-Furqan that Allah made night and day follow one another for whoever wants to remember or to be grateful. The daily cycle of sleeping and waking, light and darkness, and the moon coming and going are signs that point to the Creator, and the servants of the Merciful are those who do not fall upon His verses deaf and blind. The second reminder moves through the passage of Al-Baqarah around Ayat al-Kursi. The command to spend before a day with no trade, friendship or intercession, and the parable of the grain that grows seven ears, are meant for the moments when giving is hard; we will stand before Allah, and righteousness is reached by spending from what we love. He then turns to the man who passed a ruined town and was made to die for a hundred years. Comparing the world of 1924, with its Ottoman Empire, kings and Kaisers, to today shows how much a century changes, yet the town was restored, and Allah who says to a thing Be and it is can change any situation in the blink of an eye.

outline.heading: Interlude
Night and day in succession, for remembrance and gratitude
outline.gist: Allah made night and day follow one another for whoever wants to remember or to be thankful (Al-Furqan 62).

outline.heading: Not falling on the signs deaf and blind
outline.gist: The servants of the Merciful, when reminded of His verses, do not pass over them without hearing or seeing (Al-Furqan 73).

outline.heading: The daily cycle points to the Creator
outline.gist: Sleeping and waking, daylight, and the moon going and returning are signs; were any of it to last forever there would be no rest, and Allah uses this to remind us that He is the Creator.

outline.heading: Interlude
Spend before a day with no trade or friendship
outline.gist: The passage around Ayat al-Kursi opens with the command to spend from what Allah has provided before a day comes with no bargaining, friendship or intercession.

outline.heading: Giving when it is hard
outline.gist: The grain that grows seven ears shows how Allah multiplies spending; when giving money is difficult, remember standing before Allah and that righteousness comes by spending from what you love.

outline.heading: The man who slept a hundred years
outline.gist: He passed a ruined town and was made to die for a century; a hundred years back from today the world of the Ottoman Empire, kings and Kaisers was unrecognisable, yet the town he doubted was restored.

outline.heading: Be, and it is
outline.gist: Allah raising the bones and clothing them with flesh, and His command that a thing simply be, show that the world can be transformed in the blink of an eye and that people and conditions do change.

outline.heading: Interlude

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah
themes.note: Night, day and the moon are signs that lead the reflective person to the Creator.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: The succession of night and day is given for those who want to remember Allah or thank Him.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: Believers do not meet Allah's verses deaf and blind but stop to take them in.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Spend before the Day when nothing can be bought or borrowed, and give from what you love even when it is hard.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: The man who doubted the town could be revived came to know that Allah is able to do all things.

themes.label: Islamic history and civilization
themes.note: A century ago the Ottoman Empire and the age of kings and Kaisers shaped a world that has since changed completely.

quran.point: Night and day made to succeed each other for remembrance and gratitude.
Those who do not fall upon Allah's verses deaf and blind.
Spend before a day with no trade, friendship or intercession.
Ayat al-Kursi, named as part of the passage on spending he reflects on.
Spending in Allah's way is like a grain that grows seven ears.
Righteousness is reached only by spending from what you love, for when giving is hard.
The man who passed a ruined town, died for a hundred years and saw it revived.
Allah's command is only to say Be, and it is: everything can change at once.

stories.who: The man who passed by a ruined town (Al-Baqarah 259)
stories.point: A hundred years transform the world beyond recognition, yet Allah restored the town; He can change any situation in an instant.

takeaways: Let the passing of each night and day remind you of Allah and move you to thank Him.
Do not pass over Allah's verses and signs without stopping to reflect on them.
When giving feels hard, remember the Day when no trade or friendship helps, and give from what you love.
Trust that Allah can change any situation in an instant, however fixed it looks.

13:38.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا رُسُلࣰ ا مِّن قَبۡلِكَ وَجَعَلۡنَا لَهُمۡ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا وَذُرِّيَّةࣰۚ وَمَا كَانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَن يَأۡتِيَ بِـَٔايَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۗ لِكُلِّ أَجَلࣲ كِتَابࣱ‏
13:38.en: And verily We sent messengers (to mankind) before thee, and We appointed for them wives and offspring, and it was not (given) to any messenger that he should bring a portent save by Allah's leave. For everything there is a time prescribed

13:39.ar: يَمۡحُواْ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ وَيُثۡبِتُۖ وَعِندَهُۥٓ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ
13:39.en: Allah effaceth what He will, and establisheth (what He will), and with Him is the source of ordinance

13:40.ar: وَإِن مَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعۡضَ ٱلَّذِي نَعِدُهُمۡ أَوۡ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡبَلَٰغُ وَعَلَيۡنَا ٱلۡحِسَابُ
13:40.en: Whether We let thee see something of that which We have promised them, or make thee die (before its happening), thine is but conveyance (of the message). Ours the reckoning

13:41.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّا نَأۡتِي ٱلۡأَرۡضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنۡ أَطۡرَافِهَاۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَحۡكُمُ لَا مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكۡمِهِۦۚ وَهُوَ سَرِيعُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
13:41.en: See they not how we aim to the land, reducing it of its outlying parts? (When) Allah doometh there is none that can postpone His doom, and He is swift at reckoning

13:42.ar: وَقَدۡ مَكَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ فَلِلَّهِ ٱلۡمَكۡرُ جَمِيعࣰ اۖ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَكۡسِبُ كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲۗ وَسَيَعۡلَمُ ٱلۡكُفَّٰرُ لِمَنۡ عُقۡبَى ٱلدَّارِ
13:42.en: Those who were before them plotted; but all plotting is Allah's. He knoweth that which each soul earneth. The disbelievers will come to know for whom will be the sequel of the (heavenly) Home

13:43.ar: وَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَسۡتَ مُرۡسَلࣰ اۚ قُلۡ كَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيدَۢا بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنَكُمۡ وَمَنۡ عِندَهُۥ عِلۡمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ
13:43.en: They who disbelieve say: Thou art no messenger (of Allah). Say: Allah, and whosoever hath knowledge of the Scripture, is sufficient witness between me and you

TXHUEgkeCIg.speaker: adnan
TXHUEgkeCIg.speaker_note: concludes his own Ramadan tafsir series of Surat Al-Ra'd; mentions his years of debating and being a physician
TXHUEgkeCIg.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Ra'd: Part 8
TXHUEgkeCIg.one_line: Closing Ra'd 38-43: Allah's laws must be honoured, the Quran is this ummah's miracle, destiny is no excuse, and our only job is to do our part.
TXHUEgkeCIg.summary: He closes the surah by stressing that its theme is truth as the governing law of creation. Allah made the natural and social laws, so an ummah that is divided, uneducated and unproductive cannot expect victory; the archers at Uhud show how one breach cost years. Filling masjids is only the intention of change. Verse 38 answers the demand for an angelic messenger: prophets were human with spouses and children so they could be followed, and Muslims accept every prophet, which explains the shared core of world faiths. Miracles came only by Allah's permission, and this ummah's miracle is a book that teaches people to honour Allah's laws, now followed by some two billion. On verse 39 he distinguishes the Mother of the Book, seen by none, from the records that change with our choices and dua, and dismantles the excuse that everything is already written: you do not know what is written, so decide and act. Verse 40 tells the Prophet he may or may not live to see the outcome; his task is only to convey, and so is ours. He highlights the Prophet's grit in preaching for years to people who refused to listen. The surah ends with Allah as witness, empathy for those who struggle to leave a familiar faith, and a call to focus on one's own role.

outline.heading: Opening
Truth as the surah's governing law
outline.gist: Allah expects us to live by the laws He created; hoping for success while breaking them is cognitive dissonance.

outline.heading: Natural laws are God-made, man-described
outline.gist: Gravity and the laws of physics, chemistry and biology belong to Allah; ignoring unity, education and strength and then asking why we fail is disrespectful.

outline.heading: The archers at Uhud paid for one mistake
outline.gist: A small fraction of the army left the mountain and the Muslims paid for years, so we cannot afford to violate all of Allah's laws.

outline.heading: Coming to the masjid is the intention of change
outline.gist: Full masjids in Ramadan are only the beginning; real change must happen outside.

outline.heading: Interlude
Human messengers with spouses and children
outline.gist: Allah sends humans because you can only follow someone like you; an angel would hand the disbelievers a strong excuse.

outline.heading: Accepting every prophet and the shared story of faiths
outline.gist: Muslims accept unnamed prophets too; parallels among world religions show a common origin later altered by human hands.

outline.heading: No sign except by Allah's permission
outline.gist: The Prophet was given no physical miracle because that would imply the Quran is not enough.

outline.heading: An ummah whose miracle is a book
outline.gist: A prophet with only a book now has some two billion followers; the Quran teaches people to honour Allah's laws rather than break them for a moment.

outline.heading: Every matter has its appointed term
outline.gist: Everything runs its course and ends when Allah's decreed time arrives.

outline.heading: The Mother of the Book and the records Allah erases and confirms
outline.gist: One record holds all outcomes and is seen by none but Allah; the records angels write change with our choices and dua.

outline.heading: It is already written: then what is written?
outline.gist: Since you do not know what is written, the argument is empty; decide what you will do and that is what will be written.

outline.heading: Islam is a river, not a line
outline.gist: From his years debating he learned people cling to futile points; truth allows a range of acceptable opinions.

outline.heading: You choose, and your choice is recorded
outline.gist: Claiming no control over actions is absurd; the problem would only exist if Allah had shown us the record.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Prophet was never promised to see the outcome
outline.gist: Whether he lived to see their defeat or not, his only duty was to convey; Allah handles the reckoning.

outline.heading: Our mission regardless of results
outline.gist: Like him we must identify our job and do it whether or not it succeeds in our lifetime.

outline.heading: Interlude
Wanting every detail before doing our job
outline.gist: Like a child who will not clean his room until everything is explained, we demand assurances before acting.

outline.heading: Allah reduces the land from its edges; His decree is final
outline.gist: He takes sovereignty back from those who think they own it, and none can overturn His judgment, so focus on your piece.

outline.heading: The Prophet's grit in preaching to unwilling people
outline.gist: He spent years speaking to people who mocked and pushed him, never complaining, which made it look effortless though it was not.

cZUkPyq1xv0.one_line: Dua as an open line to Allah: speak plainly, never hang up, and an exercise in praying without masks or filters.
cZUkPyq1xv0.summary: On the last night of Ramadan 2024 the sheikh's reminders are about dua as a living conversation with Allah. He describes how the Prophet raised his hands in dua until the whiteness of his armpits showed, sleeves falling back and head lowered, the posture of someone in need before the One free of all need. He asks people to drop the formality they bring to dua and speak to Allah plainly: without You nothing in my life is real, and I have no one else to turn to. Like the old phone lines of his childhood, hard to get and never given up once connected, the line to Allah should be kept off the hook; if we hang up, Ramadan returns to let us pick it up again. The second reminder is an exercise. Everyone makes a few minutes of personal dua, then a second round repeating nothing from the first, even if that means sitting in silence. The aim is to break through the barriers we keep even before Allah and admit what we struggle with, fear and hope for, making dua beneath that inner wall rather than on top of it. He asks people to keep repeating it until they can come to Allah as they are, since a relationship with masks in it is not real.

outline.heading: The Prophet raised his hands high in dua
outline.gist: Allah responds and speaks to us through the events of our lives; he asks people to notice how the Prophet raised his hands in dua until the whiteness of his armpits showed.

outline.heading: Sleeves falling, head lowered: the posture of need
outline.gist: His hands went so high that his sleeves fell back, and he lowered his head, as the poor in need of Allah, who alone is free of need and praiseworthy.

outline.heading: Drop the formality
outline.gist: Dua is us speaking to Allah, so get rid of the formal, distant register people adopt when they address God.

outline.heading: Without You I am nothing
outline.gist: Speak to Him plainly: nothing is real without You, there is no hope of my being anything without You, and I have no one else to turn to.

outline.heading: Keep the line off the hook
outline.gist: As a child he knew phone lines that were hard to get and never given up once connected; once you pick up the line to Allah, never hang up, and if you do, Ramadan comes again to give you the chance to pick it up.

outline.heading: The one phone never to put down
outline.gist: This, not the phone in our pockets, is the line we should never put down: an ongoing conversation with Allah and a habit never to break.

outline.heading: Interlude
First round: a personal dua without filters
outline.gist: He asks everyone to take a few minutes for a personal dua about what truly matters in their life, not a generic one, dropping whatever filters they have.

outline.heading: Interlude
Why the exercise: dropping our barriers
outline.gist: We put up barriers even with Allah to avoid being vulnerable; the exercise forces us to admit what we struggle with, what we fear, what we hope for and who we really are.

outline.heading: Chipping away at the inner wall
outline.gist: With people we can say what we like, but before Allah there is no point lying; the second round must repeat nothing, sitting with nothing to say is how it starts, and dua belongs beneath the wall we built inside, not on top of it.

outline.heading: Interlude
Repeat it until the masks come off
outline.gist: Try it again over the coming months until you learn to speak to Allah in a way that is meaningful to you, removing the masks and filters we use to protect ourselves, and come to Him as you are because that is how He sees you.

outline.heading: A relationship with lies in it is not real
outline.gist: Speaking to Allah as someone you are not, when He knows it, puts deception into the relationship and makes it unreal; learn to speak to Him without it.

outline.heading: Interlude
Outro

OYJ-kVGOjDA.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 28: Quranic Reflections (Nuh to Al-Ghashiyah)
OYJ-kVGOjDA.one_line: Styles of dawah and knowing your audience, the sanctity of choice and the guilt of standing by, and a firm rejection of jinn diagnoses in favour of mental health care.
OYJ-kVGOjDA.summary: He presents Nuh and al-Jinn as two lessons in dawah: Nuh did everything right for centuries with few followers while the jinn believed without being addressed, so outcomes are not ours to control. Al-Muzzammil supplies the spiritual fuel and al-Muddaththir the teachings, the curriculum of the earliest revelation. Al-Qiyamah, al-Insan and al-Mursalat model dawah through reason, hope and fear, and a story from his harsh farming village, where a gentle imam filled the Fajr rows only after preaching about Hell, shows that preachers must know their audience. He then maps the last juz: an-Naba', an-Nazi'at and Abasa as Allah's narrative, the self as tool and obstacle, and the ethical standard; the following surahs teach that choice is sacred, recorded and narrow, and that standing by is itself a choice. Recalling his own silence before Syria fell and a colleague who lost his whole village, he says everything around us is our problem, that Muslims must stand with all the oppressed, and that children must face the consequences of their choices. From al-Jinn 9 he rejects jinn diagnoses and paid ruqyah as superstition that keeps suffering people from mental health care, and ends with al-Mursalat's sparks the size of castles.

outline.heading: Opening
The four clusters of the Mufassal
outline.gist: The first sets the choices that define a Muslim, the second organises society and relationships, and the third sets the requirements for being an ambassador of Islam.

outline.heading: An ambassador whether you like it or not
outline.gist: The moment you take the shahadah you represent the deen, so Allah lays out the ethics, spirituality and behaviour you need.

outline.heading: Nuh did everything right
outline.gist: After centuries of flawless effort, scholars put his followers at no more than about eighty-three, roughly one a decade.

outline.heading: The jinn believed without being called
outline.gist: The Prophet did not know they were listening to his night prayer, yet they believed and began reforming their community; you can do everything textbook and still fail, so do your part.

outline.heading: Al-Muzzammil: the spiritual fuel
outline.gist: To carry the burden of dawah you need prayer, night prayer, Quran recitation and dua.

outline.heading: Al-Muddaththir: what you will teach
outline.gist: The practical guidelines and body of teachings to carry to people; with al-Alaq these are among the very earliest surahs.

outline.heading: The first curriculum
outline.gist: For months the Prophet received little beyond these few surahs, which hold what he needed: fuel for himself and teachings to carry.

outline.heading: Called by that first night
outline.gist: Allah addresses him as the one wrapped up, recalling how he ran down the mountain asking to be covered; these two surahs deserve a proper study.

outline.heading: Al-Qiyamah: dawah through reason
outline.gist: Speaking to people's minds, instincts and insight, which is why the surah is filled with logic.

outline.heading: Al-Insan: dawah through hope
outline.gist: Most of the surah describes the reward Allah has hidden for the believers.

outline.heading: Al-Mursalat: dawah through fear
outline.gist: Most of the surah describes punishment, with only a small part on reward.

outline.heading: Each style carries some of the others
outline.gist: All three are valid and none is stripped of the others; dawah can lean in one direction depending on the audience.

outline.heading: A harsh village and a gentle imam
outline.gist: Around 2003 a young, sensitive and knowledgeable imam, later one of his teachers, came to his village of hard-handed farmers.

outline.heading: Love was not selling: preach about Hell
outline.gist: His sermons on love of the Prophet drew no one; the young Adnan told him love was a foreign word to men ploughing under the sun all day and urged him to speak of punishment and Allah's wrath.

outline.heading: Four rows at Fajr
outline.gist: After one fearful sermon the Fajr prayer filled four rows, and the imam looked at him knowingly.

outline.heading: Dawah is not a cookie-cutter key
outline.gist: Keep some of each style but focus according to people's capacity, psychology and context.

outline.heading: Know your audience before you speak
outline.gist: Masjids fly in speakers who know nothing about the people; knowing demographics, struggles, education, mental health, substance use and cultural backgrounds is not racism but the key to their hearts.

outline.heading: Nuh made his case: every method tried
outline.gist: Nuh tells Allah he called his people publicly, privately, in groups and alone, because had he not tried everything he would be accountable.

outline.heading: Find what moves the person in front of you
outline.gist: What moves you, especially as a parent, may not move others; assess whether someone needs arguments, hope or warning.

outline.heading: An-Naba': God's narrative of existence
outline.gist: The final cluster opens with the three elements of faith; the first is Allah's own account of creation from beginning to end.

outline.heading: An-Nazi'at: the self as tool and obstacle
outline.gist: The same nafs is both what you use to reach Allah's objective and what holds you back.

outline.heading: Abasa: the ethical standard
outline.gist: The standard the Prophet was held to and that we are held to after him.

outline.heading: At-Takwir: choice is sacred and God-given
outline.gist: Allah willed that humans have will; no one may take away anyone's freedom of thought or speech, whether they agree with Islam or not.

outline.heading: Recorded, accountable and narrow
outline.gist: The next surahs add that every choice is recorded, that you will answer for it, and that the margin of real choice is small, so choose wisely and with knowledge.

outline.heading: Doing nothing is also a choice
outline.gist: Deciding not to get involved is a choice like any other; everything around you is your problem, even when the right choice is to stay out.

outline.heading: The disadvantaged expect the advantaged to speak
outline.gist: The people of Gaza may never again see the ummah as they once did, and no one could blame them, because the advantaged said it was not their problem.

outline.heading: His poem on leaving Syria
outline.gist: Leaving a destroyed Syria he wrote that he could not blame the world for not listening, since he had not listened to Palestine or Iraq when his own house was well.

outline.heading: Carry the just causes until your last breath
outline.gist: Accepting Islam means carrying the just causes of humanity and of Muslims; the wheel of destruction rolling through the Muslim world will continue until Muslims stop living only for their own small projects.

outline.heading: We are all guilty
outline.gist: We feel others should respond only once the pain is ours; a fellow resident woke to find everyone he had ever known killed and could no longer function, and the world watched as we once did.

outline.heading: Stand with the oppressed across the board
outline.gist: Caring only about Muslim causes is a double standard; stand with truth whoever holds it, even against people of your own faith or culture.

outline.heading: Start your study with these surahs
outline.gist: Their lesson on the sanctity, recording and accountability of choice, including the choice to watch, would change how we behave.

outline.heading: Do not bail out your children
outline.gist: Let children face real, though not ruinous, consequences so they take choices seriously and can one day be trusted with personal and communal decisions.

outline.heading: Choosing is a skill; the margin is small
outline.gist: Good choices come after many wrong ones; never give your choice up to anyone or follow blindly, and remember how few options you really have.

outline.heading: Al-A'la: exalting Allah as a tool
outline.gist: The third group is the toolkit for facing life, beginning with glorifying Allah and understanding who He is.

outline.heading: Al-Ghashiyah: perseverance
outline.gist: Whatever you face now does not compare with what is coming, so persevere.

outline.heading: Interlude
The jinn can no longer listen in
outline.gist: The jinn say they used to sit and eavesdrop on the heavens but now meet a flame; it may have existed once, but it no longer does.

outline.heading: Jinn talk as superstition
outline.gist: Using jinn and magic to scare people, make them dependent and take their money is dangerous superstition; ruqyah with the Quran on yourself and loved ones is good and should be daily.

outline.heading: How do you diagnose a jinn?
outline.gist: There is no test, device or evidence for such diagnoses and no treatment plan from the Prophet beyond reciting Quran; it comes from communities lacking Islamic education.

outline.heading: Why only in my village?
outline.gist: If jinn and the evil eye worked as people think, they would not concentrate in one family, and anyone with millions of views online would melt.

outline.heading: Protecting yourself from the eye
outline.gist: The evil eye is real: recite Quran over yourself, be humble and do not show off before those who lack what you have or do not wish you well; jinn entering the brain is another matter.

outline.heading: Do not block someone from health care
outline.gist: Mental health disorders need professionals; do ruqyah on your own children, since sincerity and love matter more than another person's pronunciation.

outline.heading: Behind most ruqyah requests
outline.gist: Almost weekly parents ask him for ruqyah for a child who is clearly suffering; when he suggests a psychologist or Muslim psychiatrist they push back and shop for someone who will diagnose, while the illness worsens.

outline.heading: The verse settles it
outline.gist: The Quran removes the argument; most people simply do not read it.

outline.heading: Interlude
Sparks like castles
outline.gist: Al-Mursalat, the surah of warning, says Hell throws sparks as large as castles, which in Arabia were walls stretching for kilometres.

outline.heading: If that is the spark, what is the fire?
outline.gist: Allah describes only a few signs, sparks like a caravan of yellow camels, so we imagine the rest; these nights are when He frees people from it.

outline.heading: Outro

25:70.en: Save him who repenteth and believeth and doth righteous work; as for such, Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

2:51.ar: وَإِذۡ وَٰعَدۡنَا مُوسَىٰٓ أَرۡبَعِينَ لَيۡلَةࣰ ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذۡتُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمۡ ظَٰلِمُونَ
2:51.en: And when We did appoint for Moses forty nights (of solitude), and then ye chose the calf, when he had gone from you, and were wrong-doers

2:52.ar: ثُمَّ عَفَوۡنَا عَنكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:52.en: Then, even after that, We pardoned you in order that ye might give thanks

2:55.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهۡرَةࣰ فَأَخَذَتۡكُمُ ٱلصَّٰعِقَةُ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
2:55.en: And when ye said: O Moses! We will not believe in thee till we see Allah plainly; and even while ye gazed the lightning seized you

2:56.ar: ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَٰكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَوۡتِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:56.en: Then We revived you after your extinction, that ye might give thanks

3:152.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعۡدَهُۥٓ إِذۡ تَحُسُّونَهُم بِإِذۡنِهِۦۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلۡتُمۡ وَتَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَعَصَيۡتُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَآ أَرَىٰكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَۚ مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمۡ عَنۡهُمۡ لِيَبۡتَلِيَكُمۡۖ وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا عَنكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
3:152.en: Allah verily made good His promise unto you when ye routed them by His leave, until (the moment) when your courage failed you, and ye disagreed about the order and ye disobeyed, after He had shown you that for which ye long. Some of you desired the world, and some of you desired the Hereafter. Therefore He made you flee from them, that He might try you. Yet now He hath forgiven you. Allah is a Lord of Kindness to believers

3:155.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوۡاْ مِنكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِ إِنَّمَا ٱسۡتَزَلَّهُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ بِبَعۡضِ مَا كَسَبُواْۖ وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنۡهُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمࣱ‏
3:155.en: Lo! those of you who turned back on the day when the two hosts met, Satan alone it was who caused them to backslide, because of some of that which they have earned. Now Allah hath forgiven them. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Clement

4:43.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَنتُمۡ سُكَٰرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ تَعۡلَمُواْ مَا تَقُولُونَ وَلَا جُنُبًا إِلَّا عَابِرِي سَبِيلٍ حَتَّىٰ تَغۡتَسِلُواْۚ وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرۡضَىٰٓ أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ أَوۡ جَآءَ أَحَدࣱ مِّنكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡغَآئِطِ أَوۡ لَٰمَسۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَلَمۡ تَجِدُواْ مَآءࣰ فَتَيَمَّمُواْ صَعِيدࣰ ا طَيِّبࣰ ا فَٱمۡسَحُواْ بِوُجُوهِكُمۡ وَأَيۡدِيكُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا
4:43.en: O ye who believe! Draw not near unto prayer when ye are drunken, till ye know that which ye utter, nor when ye are polluted, save when journeying upon the road, till ye have bathed. And if ye be ill, or on a journey, or one of you cometh from the closet, or ye have touched women, and ye find not water, then go to high clean soil and rub your faces and your hands (therewith). Lo! Allah is Benign, Forgiving

58:2.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِنكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِهِم مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَٰتِهِمۡۖ إِنۡ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمۡ إِلَّا ٱلَّٰٓـِٔي وَلَدۡنَهُمۡۚ وَإِنَّهُمۡ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنكَرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِ وَزُورࣰ اۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورࣱ‏
58:2.en: Such of you as put away your wives (by saying they are as their mothers) - They are not their mothers; none are their mothers except those who gave them birth - they indeed utter an ill word and a lie. And lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

22:60.ar: ۞ذَٰلِكَۖ وَمَنۡ عَاقَبَ بِمِثۡلِ مَا عُوقِبَ بِهِۦ ثُمَّ بُغِيَ عَلَيۡهِ لَيَنصُرَنَّهُ ٱللَّهُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورࣱ‏
22:60.en: That (is so). And whoso hath retaliated with the like of that which he was made to suffer and then hath (again) been wronged, Allah will succour him. Lo! Allah verily is Mild, Forgiving

42:30.ar: وَمَآ أَصَٰبَكُم مِّن مُّصِيبَةࣲ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتۡ أَيۡدِيكُمۡ وَيَعۡفُواْ عَن كَثِيرࣲ‏
42:30.en: Whatever of misfortune striketh you, it is what your right hands have earned. And He forgiveth much

42:25.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَقۡبَلُ ٱلتَّوۡبَةَ عَنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَعۡفُواْ عَنِ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
42:25.en: And He it is Who accepteth repentance from His bondmen, and pardoneth the evil deeds, and knoweth what ye do

24:22.ar: وَلَا يَأۡتَلِ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡفَضۡلِ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤۡتُوٓاْ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَلۡيَعۡفُواْ وَلۡيَصۡفَحُوٓاْۗ أَلَا تُحِبُّونَ أَن يَغۡفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
24:22.en: And let not those who possess dignity and ease among you swear not to give to the near of kin and to the needy, and to fugitives for the cause of Allah. Let them forgive and show indulgence. Yearn ye not that Allah may forgive you? Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

3:134.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ فِي ٱلسَّرَّآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَٱلۡكَٰظِمِينَ ٱلۡغَيۡظَ وَٱلۡعَافِينَ عَنِ ٱلنَّاسِۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
3:134.en: Those who spend (of that which Allah hath given them) in ease and in adversity, those who control their wrath and are forgiving toward mankind; Allah loveth the good

12:91.ar: قَالُواْ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدۡ ءَاثَرَكَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا وَإِن كُنَّا لَخَٰطِـِٔينَ
12:91.en: They said: By Allah, verily Allah hath preferred thee above us, and we were indeed sinful

12:92.ar: قَالَ لَا تَثۡرِيبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۖ يَغۡفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۖ وَهُوَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
12:92.en: He said: Have no fear this day! May Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy

Kttjn4j-quk.speaker: adnan
Kttjn4j-quk.speaker_note: Ramadan morning Names of Allah series in his voice, given before the 27th night
Kttjn4j-quk.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-'Afuw (The Pardoner)
Kttjn4j-quk.one_line: Al-'Afuw, who erases sin entirely and replaces it with reward, and how pardoning others and leaving the past behind lets us renew ourselves.
Kttjn4j-quk.summary: On the eve of the 27th night he takes Al-'Afuw from the names of self-renewal. The root means erasing traces and surplus, so pardon moves a person from a negative to a high positive: the sin is removed, its residue wiped, Allah is pleased and reward is given. Forgiveness covers a sin that still appears in the record; pardon removes it so completely that the angel who wrote it, the person harmed and eventually you yourself forget it. That is why the Prophet taught Aisha to ask for pardon on the Night of Power. The name pairs with the Able, since pardon means something only from a position of power, and the early Muslims' hope in it came from knowing Allah, not from belittling their sins. He shows the Quran attaching pardon to the gravest failures: the calf, demanding to see Allah, the retreat at Uhud, praying drunk, and the oppression of zihar. Two applications follow. Pardon others, which is harder than forgiving because it means never raising the matter again and restoring trust, as Abu Bakr did with Mistah and the Prophet did at the conquest of Makkah. And use Allah's pardon for self-renewal: after settling what you owe people, stop carrying past sins and compete again on level ground.

outline.heading: Opening
Meaning of 'afw: erasing traces, from negative to high positive
outline.gist: Wind erasing tracks and 'give what is surplus'; His pardon removes the sin and its residue, then brings His pleasure and reward.

outline.heading: Maghfirah: the covered sin
outline.gist: Forgiveness means the sin is still in your book but stamped as concealed and forgiven.

outline.heading: Pardon: the sin is gone from the book
outline.gist: An imagined search on Judgment Day: the page is empty, the recording angel and the wronged person do not remember, and Allah says He pardoned it.

outline.heading: Aisha's dua for the Night of Power
outline.gist: O Allah, You are the Pardoner and love to pardon, so pardon me; pardon is one degree above forgiveness.

outline.heading: Paired with the Concealer and the Able
outline.gist: He conceals then pardons, and pardon is meaningful only from someone with the power to take back their right.

outline.heading: The 27th night and pardon
outline.gist: The scholars he lived with always associated this night with seeking Allah's pardon.

outline.heading: If You ask me about my sins, I will ask about Your pardon
outline.gist: Early scholars' hope grew from knowing Allah's status, unlike deluded hope that comes from not seeing one's sins as serious.

outline.heading: Pardon written on the Prophet's sword
outline.gist: Pardon whoever wronged you: the sword that restored rights was carried with the principle of pardoning once able.

outline.heading: Sins turned into good deeds
outline.gist: Pardon flips a sin into a good deed, a gift for those ashamed of their sins.

outline.heading: Pardon after the golden calf
outline.gist: Days after seeing the sea split, the Israelites worshipped a calf, and still Allah pardoned them.

outline.heading: Pardon after demanding to see Allah
outline.gist: They were struck dead, revived and pardoned.

outline.heading: Pardon twice at Uhud
outline.gist: Archers who left the mountain for the spoils and those who fled were pardoned.

outline.heading: Pardon in praying drunk and in zihar
outline.gist: Verses on prayer while intoxicated and on men oppressing wives by zihar end with Allah as Pardoner.

outline.heading: The oppressed who retaliates; calamities and much pardoned
outline.gist: Even one who goes too far in retaliating is pardoned; hardships expiate mistakes and Allah pardons much.

outline.heading: Entering Paradise without reckoning
outline.gist: He accepts repentance and pardons; seventy thousand and more enter with no account, like a legal pardon that wipes a record.

outline.heading: Big sins need pardon so they stop haunting you
outline.gist: Learn from sin and repent, but know it can be removed and even flipped; that is what this night offers.

outline.heading: Living the name 1: pardon others, as Abu Bakr did Mistah
outline.gist: Abu Bakr vowed to stop supporting the relative who spread the slander about Aisha, until the verse asked, do you not love that Allah forgive you.

outline.heading: Pardon is harder than forgiveness
outline.gist: Forgiveness reaches neutral; pardon never raises the matter again and restores the relationship, perhaps better than before.

outline.heading: The servant girl and the hot water
outline.gist: A servant's accident killed a man's child; she recited the verse on restraining anger and pardoning, and he freed her.

outline.heading: Abu Sufyan with no way back
outline.gist: After years of enmity and lying to the Prophet about the broken treaty, he was told to use the words of Yusuf's brothers, knowing the Prophet loved to follow earlier prophets.

outline.heading: No blame on you today
outline.gist: The Prophet answered with Yusuf's words, leaving no hard feelings; Abu Sufyan marvelled at his forbearance.

outline.heading: Go, you are free: the people of Makkah released
outline.gist: Those who had fought him for years were gathered and pardoned for the sake of Allah.

outline.heading: Just let it go
outline.gist: Holding a grudge only weighs on you; Allah will never let a servant outdo Him in pardoning.

outline.heading: Living the name 2: self-renewal
outline.gist: After settling what you owe people, let Allah's pardon lift the weight of past sins so you can stand straight, regain ambition and compete on level ground.

themes.note: Seek pardon on the Night of Power and the 27th night.

themes.label: Hope, fear and the balance between them
themes.note: True hope comes from knowing Allah, not from belittling sin.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: The Quran attaches pardon to the gravest failures, so no sin should keep a person from returning.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Pardoning others means never raising the matter again and restoring trust.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: The conquest of Makkah as the Prophet's supreme act of pardon.

themes.label: Self-renewal and moving past one's sins
themes.note: Allah's pardon frees a person from the burden of the past to strive again.

Pardoning wrong, for Allah is Pardoning and Able
Allah replaces their evil deeds with good
The calf worshipped in forty nights, then We pardoned you so you might be grateful
Demanding to see Allah, struck dead and revived
At Uhud some wanted the world, then He pardoned you
Those who turned back on the day the armies met were pardoned
Do not approach prayer while intoxicated; Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving
Zihar is a harmful lie, yet Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving
The wronged who retaliates and is wronged again will be helped; Allah is Pardoning
Calamities come from what your hands earned, and He pardons much
He accepts repentance from His servants and pardons sins
Let them pardon and overlook; do you not love that Allah forgive you
Those who restrain anger and pardon people; Allah loves the doers of good
Yusuf's brothers' admission and his reply, 'no blame on you today'

hadith.gist: Aisha asked what to say if she found the Night of Power; the Prophet taught: O Allah, You are Pardoning and love to pardon, so pardon me
Written on the Prophet's sword: pardon whoever wrongs you
Seventy thousand of the Prophet's nation will enter Paradise without reckoning, with seventy thousand more for every thousand
At the conquest of Makkah the Prophet told the Quraysh to go, for they were free

maxims: Forgiveness is negative to neutral; pardon is negative to high positive
It was not as if it didn't happen; it didn't happen
If You ask about my sins, I'll ask about Your pardon
Just let it go

stories.who: An imagined search for a pardoned sin on Judgment Day
stories.point: Pardon removes a sin so completely that no one, including you, remembers it.

stories.who: The Israelites and the golden calf
stories.point: Even worshipping a calf after great miracles was pardoned.

stories.who: Abu Bakr and Mistah
stories.point: Pardoning someone who wronged your family means resuming kindness, hoping for Allah's forgiveness.

stories.who: The servant girl and the scalding water
stories.point: Pardoning at a moment of devastating loss is the height of excellence.

stories.who: Abu Sufyan at the conquest of Makkah
stories.point: The Prophet pardoned a man who had wronged him for decades with Yusuf's words, leaving no hard feelings.

contemporary: Legal pardons that clear a criminal record
Curling
takeaways: Ask Allah for pardon on the remaining nights with the dua taught to Aisha
Pardon someone who wronged you: never raise it again and restore trust
Settle the rights you owe people first, since Allah's pardon does not cover them
Let Allah's pardon free you from carrying past sins and renew your ambition

60:9.ar: إِنَّمَا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ قَٰتَلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَأَخۡرَجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ وَظَٰهَرُواْ عَلَىٰٓ إِخۡرَاجِكُمۡ أَن تَوَلَّوۡهُمۡۚ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّهُمۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
60:9.en: Allah forbiddeth you only those who warred against you on account of religion and have driven you out from your homes and helped to drive you out, that ye make friends of them. Whosoever maketh friends of them - (All) such are wrong-doers

62:5.ar: مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ حُمِّلُواْ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةَ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَحۡمِلُوهَا كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡحِمَارِ يَحۡمِلُ أَسۡفَارَۢاۚ بِئۡسَ مَثَلُ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
62:5.en: The likeness of those who are entrusted with the Law of Moses, yet apply it not, is as the likeness of the ass carrying books. Wretched is the likeness of folk who deny the revelations of Allah. And Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

65:7.ar: لِيُنفِقۡ ذُو سَعَةࣲ مِّن سَعَتِهِۦۖ وَمَن قُدِرَ عَلَيۡهِ رِزۡقُهُۥ فَلۡيُنفِقۡ مِمَّآ ءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُۚ لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا مَآ ءَاتَىٰهَاۚ سَيَجۡعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡدَ عُسۡرࣲ يُسۡرࣰ ا
65:7.en: Let him who hath abundance spend of his abundance, and he whose provision is measured, let him spend of that which Allah hath given him. Allah asketh naught of any soul save that which He hath given it. Allah will vouchsafe, after hardship, ease

67:22.ar: أَفَمَن يَمۡشِي مُكِبًّا عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦٓ أَهۡدَىٰٓ أَمَّن يَمۡشِي سَوِيًّا عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
67:22.en: Is he who goeth groping on his face more rightly guided, or he who walketh upright on a straight road

68:42.ar: يَوۡمَ يُكۡشَفُ عَن سَاقࣲ وَيُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ فَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ
68:42.en: On the day when it befalleth in earnest, and they are ordered to prostrate themselves but are not able

68:43.ar: خَٰشِعَةً أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ تَرۡهَقُهُمۡ ذِلَّةࣱۖ وَقَدۡ كَانُواْ يُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمۡ سَٰلِمُونَ
68:43.en: With eyes downcast, abasement stupefying them. And they had been summoned to prostrate themselves while they were yet unhurt

69:44.en: And if he had invented false sayings concerning Us

60:8.ar: لَّا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يُقَٰتِلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَلَمۡ يُخۡرِجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ أَن تَبَرُّوهُمۡ وَتُقۡسِطُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُقۡسِطِينَ
60:8.en: Allah forbiddeth you not those who warred not against you on account of religion and drove you not out from your homes, that ye should show them kindness and deal justly with them. Lo! Allah loveth the just dealers

61:10.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ تِجَٰرَةࣲ تُنجِيكُم مِّنۡ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
61:10.en: O ye who believe! Shall I show you a commerce that will save you from a painful doom

61:11.ar: تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَتُجَٰهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ بِأَمۡوَٰلِكُمۡ وَأَنفُسِكُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
61:11.en: Ye should believe in Allah and His messenger, and should strive for the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if ye did but know

61:4.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِۦ صَفࣰّ ا كَأَنَّهُم بُنۡيَٰنࣱ مَّرۡصُوصࣱ‏
61:4.en: Lo! Allah loveth them who battle for His cause in ranks, as if they were a solid structure

UpnLNYJJWFs.speaker: adnan
UpnLNYJJWFs.speaker_note: Ramadan 2024 Quranic Reflections series he leads, continuing his Mufassal cluster framework
UpnLNYJJWFs.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 27: Quranic Reflections (Al-Mumtahinah to Al-Ma'arij)
UpnLNYJJWFs.one_line: The Madani organising surahs: relations with non-Muslims and refusing normalisation, the social contract, leadership, carrying the Quran, spousal finances, walking upright, and the reversed prostration.
UpnLNYJJWFs.summary: On the 27th night he cautions against neglecting the other nights, then surveys the Madani organisational surahs. Al-Mumtahinah sets how Muslims treat non-Muslims: love and compassion except toward those who attack their faith or expel them. As-Saff lays out the social contract: no Muslim floats alone, and everyone is accountable for their part in the community. Al-Jumu'ah reveals a built-in system of leadership; he admits the community has no clear collective goal, argues that even poor leadership beats none, and distinguishes leaders who do the work from bosses. He notes al-Munafiqun, at-Taghabun, at-Talaq and at-Tahrim, and frames the next juz as what a Muslim ambassador needs. On al-Mumtahinah 9 he insists the verse leaves no room to normalise relations with an apartheid state oppressing Muslims, while stressing that Muslims love humanity and protect others. The donkey carrying books warns against owning the Quran without living it. At-Talaq 7 grounds marital finances in the husband's duty, calls for just negotiation when a wife also earns, and warns against delaying marriage for wealth. Al-Mulk contrasts walking face-down with walking upright and balanced, and al-Qalam describes the Day when those too proud to prostrate find their backs will not bend.

outline.heading: Opening
The 27th night: revered, but not the only night
outline.gist: Many companions and scholars considered it Laylat al-Qadr and it carries status everywhere, but focusing on it while ignoring the other nights is unhealthy.

outline.heading: The Madani cluster that organises Muslim life
outline.gist: From al-Mujadilah onward the surahs organise aspects of life, including relations with non-Muslims.

outline.heading: Al-Mumtahinah: how we view and treat non-Muslims
outline.gist: In a diverse world this matters greatly: Muslims show love, mercy and compassion to non-Muslims, refusing alliance only with those who oppress them, expel them, deny their religious freedom or help others do so.

outline.heading: As-Saff: the social contract
outline.gist: The surah contains a contract and explains what an individual owes the group, a question many Muslims do not realise they will be asked about.

outline.heading: No Muslim floats alone
outline.gist: Withdrawing from community is acceptable only if you are the last Muslim, rejected by all and under threat; otherwise non-involvement reflects a misunderstanding of the faith.

outline.heading: Part of the line
outline.gist: The name means a rank: everyone is equally valued and equally responsible for carrying the message, standing against corruption and refusing oppression until meeting Allah.

outline.heading: Al-Jumu'ah: a built-in system of leadership
outline.gist: Wherever a few Muslims gather they build a masjid and hold Jumuah; historically the leader, not the scholar, gave the khutbah because it is about direction, and we have ruined this remarkably.

outline.heading: What is our goal as a community?
outline.gist: Young people ask what Muslims are trying to achieve here and he has no answer; keeping the masjid full is not a goal, and without leadership the community runs like a headless chicken.

outline.heading: Lousy leadership beats none
outline.gist: Even poor leadership goes somewhere and can correct course when it hits a wall; without it all the community's energy disperses uselessly.

outline.heading: Leaders, followers and bosses
outline.gist: Leadership needs followers, but in our communities everyone wants to lead; leading means doing the work and sacrificing time, family and sleep, while bosses only give orders.

outline.heading: Al-Munafiqun: the group in the middle
outline.gist: Between Muslim and non-Muslim are those halfway in; there is no criterion to pinpoint them and doing so is arrogant, so the real question is how to make sure we are not among them.

outline.heading: At-Taghabun: why we follow the rulings
outline.gist: A short, deeply spiritual surah reminding that rituals and laws are followed because Allah commanded them.

outline.heading: At-Talaq: founding and ending a family
outline.gist: Rights and laws of men and women in marriage, the rules before building a family and when it ends.

outline.heading: At-Tahrim: life within the family
outline.gist: The laws governing what happens inside the family.

outline.heading: Juz Tabarak: what a Muslim ambassador needs
outline.gist: Al-Mulk teaches knowledge, al-Qalam ethics, al-Haqqah connection to Allah and al-Ma'arij behaviour; whoever you are, people see Islam through you.

outline.heading: Interlude
Allah forbids alliance only with those who fight your faith
outline.gist: The prohibition is specific: those who fight your right to faith, expel you from your land or help others expel you.

outline.heading: Not war, but no alliance: normalisation
outline.gist: The verse does not demand war, but you may not take such people as allies even if you cannot fight them; normalising relations with an apartheid state long oppressing Muslims is exactly this, and those who do it are the wrongdoers.

outline.heading: A verse with almost no room for another reading
outline.gist: Its terms are specific rather than general, leaving little room for interpretation; he challenges anyone to read it otherwise and assumes those who normalise do not read the Quran.

outline.heading: Muslims love humanity
outline.gist: Muslims are not bloodthirsty: they love the human race, all prophets and books, and welcome non-Muslims to live among them with protected rights and places of worship.

outline.heading: If refusing oppression is a crime, I am guilty
outline.gist: Muslims refuse oppression and persecution and will never normalise with oppressors even if none are left; it is not about numbers or strength, because Allah owns our lives.

outline.heading: The donkey carrying books
outline.gist: A rare parable likening people to an animal: those entrusted with scripture who did not carry it, meaning understand, practise and implement it.

outline.heading: Not the Quran hanging in your car
outline.gist: Owning a beautiful copy on the wall or the mirror is not carrying the book if you do not live by it.

outline.heading: Leadership turns the book into practice
outline.gist: Allah brings reform through leadership more than through the text alone; without it people hold knowledge they cannot use, like the donkey.

outline.heading: Does the Quran define you?
outline.gist: You may recite or even memorise it without carrying its message; if it does not define you, ask what does.

outline.heading: Interlude
Spend according to your means
outline.gist: This verse summarises the civil law detailed elsewhere: the husband spends from what he has, much or little.

outline.heading: Interlude
The husband is financially responsible
outline.gist: He is not asked to pay beyond his means, but his wife is not obliged to spend her wealth; if she does, there must be an arrangement that gives her something in return.

outline.heading: Why the roles are distinguished
outline.gist: Spending on the household feels like an extra to most women, as dishes and garbage feel extra to most men; Islam makes him breadwinner and her the keeper of home and children as the starting point.

outline.heading: When she earns too: negotiate a just balance
outline.gist: If a physician wife pays half the household costs, he must take on half her role or resentment will follow; he sees imbalanced households in the community exploiting both women and men.

outline.heading: After hardship, ease: build a marriage from little
outline.gist: Allah promises ease after difficulty; starting poor together builds a bond that waiting until you are well off removes.

outline.heading: Sounding the alarm on delayed marriage
outline.gist: A man should earn before marrying, but postponing marriage into the thirties for wealth, in a society with no sense of halal and haram, is a dangerous slope.

outline.heading: Interlude
Face down or walking upright
outline.gist: Is the one walking with his face tilted to the ground better guided than the one walking balanced on a straight path?

outline.heading: Not better people, a better walk of life
outline.gist: Being guided does not make us better than others; it means our path is better, which should make us guard it and be grateful.

outline.heading: Lift your head
outline.gist: The face-down walker sees only what is close and temporary; reaching a destination requires zooming out from petty details you will forget in a few years.

outline.heading: Know what is next from you
outline.gist: You cannot control what Allah decrees for you, but you can know who you are and where you are going; the face-down walker has no warning system and the next wave knocks him over.

outline.heading: Tranquillity versus tumbling
outline.gist: Allah's guidance gives calm, clarity and balance to recover your path in hardship, while others tumble along at the mercy of luck.

outline.heading: In this world a raised head means dignity
outline.gist: Standing with your head high signals dignity and a lowered face signals humiliation; that is how this life works.

outline.heading: The unveiling: everything reverses
outline.gist: On Judgment Day the laws change; the phrase about the shin being bared is an Arabic expression for an enormous, indescribable event, which he leaves unspecified as Allah did.

outline.heading: Backs that will not bend
outline.gist: All are called to prostrate and some cannot, their backs rigid like metal; the dignified one is the one who reaches the ground, while those left standing tall are humiliated.

outline.heading: Called to prostrate while they were well
outline.gist: They were invited to prostrate when healthy and held their heads high instead; ask Allah to let you go down quickly that Day.

outline.heading: Al-Haqqah: had he fabricated
outline.gist: He begins the verse establishing that the Prophet did not invent the message.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Honour the 27th night without neglecting the other nights.

themes.label: Tolerance, pluralism and dealing with difference
themes.note: Love and compassion toward non-Muslims except those who persecute or expel Muslims.

themes.label: The Islamic social contract: rights and obligations of belonging
themes.note: Each Muslim is accountable for his involvement in the community; no one floats alone.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: Jumuah embeds leadership; the community lacks a goal and needs leaders who work, not bosses.

themes.label: Hypocrisy (nifaq)
themes.note: The half-in group cannot be identified by others; ensure you are not among them.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: A Muslim ambassador needs knowledge, ethics, connection to Allah and behaviour.

themes.label: Alliances and loyalty: whom Muslims stand with
themes.note: No alliance with those who fight Muslims' faith or expel them, which rules out normalisation.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: Normalising with an apartheid state oppressing Muslims contradicts a clear verse.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Muslims love humanity and protect others, but refusing oppression is non-negotiable.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: Carrying the book means living it; otherwise we resemble the donkey carrying books.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: The husband's financial duty, just negotiation when both earn, and the danger of delaying marriage for wealth.

themes.label: Guidance (hidayah)
themes.note: Guidance is walking upright and balanced, seeing the path beyond petty details.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: On Judgment Day dignity reverses: those who refused to prostrate in life cannot do so.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: Prostrate now, while healthy, so you can prostrate that Day.

quran.point: Kindness and justice toward non-Muslims who do not fight or expel Muslims.
The contract or trade within as-Saff that defines what the believer gives.
Believers standing in a rank, behind the surah's name.

maxims: Lousy leadership is better than no leadership
Leaders do the work; bosses are useless
You are a Muslim ambassador whether you like it or not
If refusing oppression is a crime, then I am guilty
Don't play around with justice in relationships
Not what comes to you, but what's next from you
contemporary: Normalisation of relations with an apartheid state that has long oppressed Muslims
A Muslim community with no stated collective goal beyond filling the masjid
Imbalanced households where wives or husbands are taken advantage of
Muslims postponing marriage into their thirties to accumulate wealth
Increasingly diverse societies where Muslims live alongside many faiths
takeaways: Take an active, accountable part in your community instead of floating alone
Lead by doing the work, and be willing to follow good leadership
Live the Quran rather than displaying it
Start marital finances from the husband's duty and negotiate fairly when both earn; do not delay marriage for wealth
Lift your head beyond petty details, and prostrate now while you are able

2:2.ar: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَۛ فِيهِۛ هُدࣰ ى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ
2:2.en: This is the Scripture whereof there is no doubt, a guidance unto those who ward off (evil)

2:3.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
2:3.en: Who believe in the Unseen, and establish worship, and spend of that We have bestowed upon them

2:4.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبۡلِكَ وَبِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمۡ يُوقِنُونَ
2:4.en: And who believe in that which is revealed unto thee (Muhammad) and that which was revealed before thee, and are certain of the Hereafter

2:5.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدࣰ ى مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
2:5.en: These depend on guidance from their Lord. These are the successful

2:6.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
2:6.en: As for the Disbelievers, Whether thou warn them or thou warn them not it is all one for them; they believe not

2:7.ar: خَتَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ وَعَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِمۡۖ وَعَلَىٰٓ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ غِشَٰوَةࣱۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
2:7.en: Allah hath sealed their hearing and their hearts, and on their eyes there is a covering. Theirs will be an awful doom

2:8.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَبِٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَمَا هُم بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ
2:8.en: And of mankind are some who say: We believe in Allah and the Last Day, when they believe not

2:9.ar: يُخَٰدِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَمَا يَخۡدَعُونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَمَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
2:9.en: They think to beguile Allah and those who believe, and they beguile none save themselves; but they perceive not

2:10.ar: فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضࣱ فَزَادَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَرَضࣰ اۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمُۢ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡذِبُونَ
2:10.en: In their hearts is a disease, and Allah increaseth their disease. A painful doom is theirs because they lie

2:11.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ لَا تُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا نَحۡنُ مُصۡلِحُونَ
2:11.en: And when it is said unto them: Make not mischief in the earth, they say: We are peacemakers only

2:12.ar: أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدُونَ وَلَٰكِن لَّا يَشۡعُرُونَ
2:12.en: Are not they indeed the mischief-makers? But they perceive not

2:13.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ ءَامِنُواْ كَمَآ ءَامَنَ ٱلنَّاسُ قَالُوٓاْ أَنُؤۡمِنُ كَمَآ ءَامَنَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُۗ أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ وَلَٰكِن لَّا يَعۡلَمُونَ
2:13.en: And when it is said unto them: believe as the people believe, they say: shall we believe as the foolish believe? are not they indeed the foolish? But they know not

2:14.ar: وَإِذَا لَقُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ شَيَٰطِينِهِمۡ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا مَعَكُمۡ إِنَّمَا نَحۡنُ مُسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
2:14.en: And when they fall in with those who believe, they say: We believe; but when they go apart to their devils they declare: Lo! we are with you; verily we did but mock

2:15.ar: ٱللَّهُ يَسۡتَهۡزِئُ بِهِمۡ وَيَمُدُّهُمۡ فِي طُغۡيَٰنِهِمۡ يَعۡمَهُونَ
2:15.en: Allah (Himself) doth mock them, leaving them to wander blindly on in their contumacy

2:16.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشۡتَرَوُاْ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ فَمَا رَبِحَت تِّجَٰرَتُهُمۡ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُهۡتَدِينَ
2:16.en: These are they who purchase error at the price of guidance, so their commerce doth not prosper, neither are they guided

2:17.ar: مَثَلُهُمۡ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِي ٱسۡتَوۡقَدَ نَارࣰ ا فَلَمَّآ أَضَآءَتۡ مَا حَوۡلَهُۥ ذَهَبَ ٱللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمۡ وَتَرَكَهُمۡ فِي ظُلُمَٰتࣲ لَّا يُبۡصِرُونَ
2:17.en: Their likeness is as the likeness of one who kindleth fire, and when it sheddeth its light around him Allah taketh away their light and leaveth them in darkness, where they cannot see

2:18.ar: صُمُّۢ بُكۡمٌ عُمۡيࣱ فَهُمۡ لَا يَرۡجِعُونَ
2:18.en: Deaf, dumb and blind; and they return not

2:19.ar: أَوۡ كَصَيِّبࣲ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَٰتࣱ وَرَعۡدࣱ وَبَرۡقࣱ يَجۡعَلُونَ أَصَٰبِعَهُمۡ فِيٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۚ وَٱللَّهُ مُحِيطُۢ بِٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:19.en: Or like a rainstorm from the sky, wherein is darkness, thunder and the flash of lightning. They thrust their fingers in their ears by reason of the thunder-claps, for fear of death, Allah encompasseth the disbelievers (in His guidance, His omniscience and His omnipotence)

2:20.ar: يَكَادُ ٱلۡبَرۡقُ يَخۡطَفُ أَبۡصَٰرَهُمۡۖ كُلَّمَآ أَضَآءَ لَهُم مَّشَوۡاْ فِيهِ وَإِذَآ أَظۡلَمَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ قَامُواْۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمۡعِهِمۡ وَأَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
2:20.en: The lightning almost snatcheth away their sight from them. As often as it flasheth forth for them they walk therein, and when it darkeneth against them they stand still. If Allah willed, He could destroy their hearing and their sight. Lo! Allah is able to do all things

2:21.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱعۡبُدُواْ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
2:21.en: O mankind! worship your Lord, Who hath created you and those before you, so that ye may ward off (evil)

2:22.ar: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِرَٰشࣰ ا وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءࣰ وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزۡقࣰ ا لَّكُمۡۖ فَلَا تَجۡعَلُواْ لِلَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا وَأَنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:22.en: Who hath appointed the earth a resting-place for you, and the sky a canopy; and causeth water to pour down from the sky, thereby producing fruits as food for you. And do not set up rivals to Allah when ye know (better)

2:23.ar: وَإِن كُنتُمۡ فِي رَيۡبࣲ مِّمَّا نَزَّلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا فَأۡتُواْ بِسُورَةࣲ مِّن مِّثۡلِهِۦ وَٱدۡعُواْ شُهَدَآءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:23.en: And if ye are in doubt concerning that which We reveal unto Our slave (Muhammad), then produce a surah of the like thereof, and call your witness beside Allah if ye are truthful

2:24.ar: فَإِن لَّمۡ تَفۡعَلُواْ وَلَن تَفۡعَلُواْ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِي وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلۡحِجَارَةُۖ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:24.en: And if ye do it not - and ye can never do it - then guard yourselves against the Fire prepared for disbelievers, whose fuel is of men and stones

2:25.ar: وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُۖ كُلَّمَا رُزِقُواْ مِنۡهَا مِن ثَمَرَةࣲ رِّزۡقࣰ ا قَالُواْ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي رُزِقۡنَا مِن قَبۡلُۖ وَأُتُواْ بِهِۦ مُتَشَٰبِهࣰ اۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِيهَآ أَزۡوَٰجࣱ مُّطَهَّرَةࣱۖ وَهُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:25.en: And give glad tidings (O Muhammad) unto those who believe and do good works; that theirs are Gardens underneath which rivers flow; as often as they are regaled with food of the fruit thereof, they say: this is what was given us aforetime; and it is given to them in resemblance. There for them are pure companions; there for ever they abide

2:26.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَسۡتَحۡيِۦٓ أَن يَضۡرِبَ مَثَلࣰ ا مَّا بَعُوضَةࣰ فَمَا فَوۡقَهَاۚ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَيَقُولُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلࣰ اۘ يُضِلُّ بِهِۦ كَثِيرࣰ ا وَيَهۡدِي بِهِۦ كَثِيرࣰ اۚ وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
2:26.en: Lo! Allah disdaineth not to coin the similitude even of a gnat. Those who believe know that it is the truth from their Lord; but those who disbelieve say: What doth Allah wish (to teach) by such a similitude? He misleadeth many thereby, and He guideth many thereby; and He misleadeth thereby only miscreants

2:27.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَنقُضُونَ عَهۡدَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مِيثَٰقِهِۦ وَيَقۡطَعُونَ مَآ أَمَرَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦٓ أَن يُوصَلَ وَيُفۡسِدُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
2:27.en: Those who break the covenant of Allah after ratifying it, and sever that which Allah ordered to be joined, and (who) make mischief in the earth: Those are they who are the losers

2:28.ar: كَيۡفَ تَكۡفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَكُنتُمۡ أَمۡوَٰتࣰ ا فَأَحۡيَٰكُمۡۖ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُحۡيِيكُمۡ ثُمَّ إِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
2:28.en: How disbelieve ye in Allah when ye were dead and He gave life to you! Then He will give you death, then life again, and then unto Him ye will return

2:29.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَسَوَّىٰهُنَّ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲۚ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
2:29.en: He it is Who created for you all that is in the earth. Then turned He to the heaven, and fashioned it as seven heavens. And He is knower of all things

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

2:31.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:31.en: And He taught Adam all the names, then showed them to the angels, saying: Inform Me of the names of these, if ye are truthful

2:32.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمۡتَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:32.en: They said: Be glorified! We have no knowledge saving that which Thou hast taught us. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower, the Wise

2:33.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئۡهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡۖ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡ قَالَ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ غَيۡبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مَا تُبۡدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡتُمُونَ
2:33.en: He said: O Adam! Inform them of their names, and when he had informed them of their names, He said: Did I not tell you that I know the secret of the heavens and the earth? And I know that which ye disclose and which ye hide

2:34.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأٓدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:34.en: And when We said unto the angels: Prostrate yourselves before Adam, they fell prostrate, all save Iblis. He demurred through pride, and so became a disbeliever

2:35.ar: وَقُلۡنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسۡكُنۡ أَنتَ وَزَوۡجُكَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنۡهَا رَغَدًا حَيۡثُ شِئۡتُمَا وَلَا تَقۡرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:35.en: And We said: O Adam! Dwell thou and thy wife in the Garden, and eat ye freely (of the fruits) thereof where ye will; but come not nigh this tree lest ye become wrong-doers

2:36.ar: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ عَنۡهَا فَأَخۡرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِۖ وَقُلۡنَا ٱهۡبِطُواْ بَعۡضُكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوࣱّۖ وَلَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُسۡتَقَرࣱّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينࣲ‏
2:36.en: But Satan caused them to deflect therefrom and expelled them from the (happy) state in which they were; and We said: Fall down, one of you a foe unto the other! There shall be for you on earth a habitation and provision for a time

2:37.ar: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتࣲ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:37.en: Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him. Lo! He is the relenting, the Merciful

2:38.ar: قُلۡنَا ٱهۡبِطُواْ مِنۡهَا جَمِيعࣰ اۖ فَإِمَّا يَأۡتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدࣰ ى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
2:38.en: We said: Go down, all of you, from hence; but verily there cometh unto you from Me a guidance; and whoso followeth My guidance, there shall no fear come upon them neither shall they grieve

2:39.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَكَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:39.en: But they who disbelieve, and deny Our revelations, such are rightful Peoples of the Fire. They will abide therein

2:40.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتِيَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَوۡفُواْ بِعَهۡدِيٓ أُوفِ بِعَهۡدِكُمۡ وَإِيَّٰيَ فَٱرۡهَبُونِ
2:40.en: O Children of Israel! Remember My favour wherewith I favoured you, and fulfil your (part of the) covenant, I shall fulfil My (part of the) covenant, and fear Me

2:41.ar: وَءَامِنُواْ بِمَآ أَنزَلۡتُ مُصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا مَعَكُمۡ وَلَا تَكُونُوٓاْ أَوَّلَ كَافِرِۭ بِهِۦۖ وَلَا تَشۡتَرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِي ثَمَنࣰ ا قَلِيلࣰ ا وَإِيَّٰيَ فَٱتَّقُونِ
2:41.en: And believe in that which I reveal, confirming that which ye possess already (of the Scripture), and be not first to disbelieve therein, and part not with My revelations for a trifling price, and keep your duty unto Me

2:42.ar: وَلَا تَلۡبِسُواْ ٱلۡحَقَّ بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ وَتَكۡتُمُواْ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَأَنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:42.en: Confound not truth with falsehood, nor knowingly conceal the truth

2:43.ar: وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱرۡكَعُواْ مَعَ ٱلرَّٰكِعِينَ
2:43.en: Establish worship, pay the poor-due, and bow your heads with those who bow (in worship)

2:44.ar: ۞أَتَأۡمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلۡبِرِّ وَتَنسَوۡنَ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ تَتۡلُونَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
2:44.en: Enjoin ye righteousness upon mankind while ye yourselves forget (to practise it)? And ye are readers of the Scripture! Have ye then no sense

2:45.ar: وَٱسۡتَعِينُواْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِۚ وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلۡخَٰشِعِينَ
2:45.en: Seek help in patience and prayer; and truly it is hard save for the humble-minded

2:46.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُواْ رَبِّهِمۡ وَأَنَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
2:46.en: Who know that they will have to meet their Lord, and that unto Him they are returning

2:47.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتِيَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَنِّي فَضَّلۡتُكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
2:47.en: O Children of Israel! Remember My favour wherewith I favoured you and how I preferred you to (all) creatures

2:48.ar: وَٱتَّقُواْ يَوۡمࣰ ا لَّا تَجۡزِي نَفۡسٌ عَن نَّفۡسࣲ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يُقۡبَلُ مِنۡهَا شَفَٰعَةࣱ وَلَا يُؤۡخَذُ مِنۡهَا عَدۡلࣱ وَلَا هُمۡ يُنصَرُونَ
2:48.en: And guard yourselves against a day when no soul will in aught avail another, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be received from it, nor will they be helped

2:49.ar: وَإِذۡ نَجَّيۡنَٰكُم مِّنۡ ءَالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ يَسُومُونَكُمۡ سُوٓءَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبۡنَآءَكُمۡ وَيَسۡتَحۡيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمۡۚ وَفِي ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ عَظِيمࣱ‏
2:49.en: And (remember) when We did deliver you from Pharaoh's folk, who were afflicting you with dreadful torment, slaying your sons and sparing your women: that was a tremendous trial from your Lord

2:50.ar: وَإِذۡ فَرَقۡنَا بِكُمُ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَنجَيۡنَٰكُمۡ وَأَغۡرَقۡنَآ ءَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
2:50.en: And when We brought you through the sea and rescued you, and drowned the folk of Pharaoh in your sight

2:51.ar: وَإِذۡ وَٰعَدۡنَا مُوسَىٰٓ أَرۡبَعِينَ لَيۡلَةࣰ ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذۡتُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمۡ ظَٰلِمُونَ
2:51.en: And when We did appoint for Moses forty nights (of solitude), and then ye chose the calf, when he had gone from you, and were wrong-doers

2:52.ar: ثُمَّ عَفَوۡنَا عَنكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:52.en: Then, even after that, We pardoned you in order that ye might give thanks

2:53.ar: وَإِذۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ
2:53.en: And when We gave unto Moses the Scripture and the criterion (of right and wrong), that ye might be led aright

2:54.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنَّكُمۡ ظَلَمۡتُمۡ أَنفُسَكُم بِٱتِّخَاذِكُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ فَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمۡ فَٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمۡ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:54.en: And when Moses said unto his people: O my people! Ye have wronged yourselves by your choosing of the calf (for worship) so turn in penitence to your Creator, and kill (the guilty) yourselves. That will be best for you with your Creator and He will relent toward you. Lo! He is the Relenting, the Merciful

2:55.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهۡرَةࣰ فَأَخَذَتۡكُمُ ٱلصَّٰعِقَةُ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
2:55.en: And when ye said: O Moses! We will not believe in thee till we see Allah plainly; and even while ye gazed the lightning seized you

2:56.ar: ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَٰكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَوۡتِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:56.en: Then We revived you after your extinction, that ye might give thanks

2:57.ar: وَظَلَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡغَمَامَ وَأَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلۡوَىٰۖ كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡۚ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ
2:57.en: And We caused the white cloud to overshadow you and sent down on you the manna and the quails, (saying): Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you - they wronged Us not, but they did wrong themselves

2:58.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا ٱدۡخُلُواْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةَ فَكُلُواْ مِنۡهَا حَيۡثُ شِئۡتُمۡ رَغَدࣰ ا وَٱدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡبَابَ سُجَّدࣰ ا وَقُولُواْ حِطَّةࣱ نَّغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ خَطَٰيَٰكُمۡۚ وَسَنَزِيدُ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
2:58.en: And when We said: Go into this township and eat freely of that which is therein, and enter the gate prostrate, and say: "Repentance." We will forgive you your sins and will increase (reward) for the right-doers

2:59.ar: فَبَدَّلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ قَوۡلًا غَيۡرَ ٱلَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمۡ فَأَنزَلۡنَا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ رِجۡزࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡسُقُونَ
2:59.en: But those who did wrong changed the word which had been told them for another saying, and We sent down upon the evil-doers wrath from heaven for their evil-doing

2:60.ar: ۞وَإِذِ ٱسۡتَسۡقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ فَقُلۡنَا ٱضۡرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلۡحَجَرَۖ فَٱنفَجَرَتۡ مِنۡهُ ٱثۡنَتَا عَشۡرَةَ عَيۡنࣰ اۖ قَدۡ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسࣲ مَّشۡرَبَهُمۡۖ كُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ مِن رِّزۡقِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تَعۡثَوۡاْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُفۡسِدِينَ
2:60.en: And when Moses asked for water for his people, We said: Smite with thy staff the rock. And there gushed out therefrom twelve springs (so that) each tribe knew their drinking-place. Eat and drink of that which Allah hath provided, and do not act corruptly, making mischief in the earth

2:61.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصۡبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامࣲ وَٰحِدࣲ فَٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخۡرِجۡ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ مِنۢ بَقۡلِهَا وَقِثَّآئِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَاۖ قَالَ أَتَسۡتَبۡدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِي هُوَ أَدۡنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِي هُوَ خَيۡرٌۚ ٱهۡبِطُواْ مِصۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلۡتُمۡۗ وَضُرِبَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ وَٱلۡمَسۡكَنَةُ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبࣲ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَواْ وَّكَانُواْ يَعۡتَدُونَ
2:61.en: And when ye said: O Moses! We are weary of one kind of food; so call upon thy Lord for us that He bring forth for us of that which the earth groweth - of its herbs and its cucumbers and its corn and its lentils and its onions. He said: Would ye exchange that which is higher for that which is lower? Go down to settled country, thus ye shall get that which ye demand. And humiliation and wretchedness were stamped upon them and they were visited with wrath from Allah. That was because they disbelieved in Allah's revelations and slew the prophets wrongfully. That was for their disobedience and transgression

3:2.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُ
3:2.en: Allah! There is no god save Him, the Alive, the Eternal

3:3.ar: نَزَّلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ مُصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ وَأَنزَلَ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةَ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلَ
3:3.en: He hath revealed unto thee (Muhammad) the Scripture with truth, confirming that which was (revealed) before it, even as He revealed the Torah and the Gospel

3:4.ar: مِن قَبۡلُ هُدࣰ ى لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَنزَلَ ٱلۡفُرۡقَانَۗ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدࣱۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزࣱ ذُو ٱنتِقَامٍ
3:4.en: Aforetime, for a guidance to mankind; and hath revealed the Criterion (of right and wrong). Lo! those who disbelieve the revelations of Allah, theirs will be a heavy doom. Allah is Mighty, Able to Requite (the wrong)

3:5.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَخۡفَىٰ عَلَيۡهِ شَيۡءࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ
3:5.en: Lo! nothing in the earth or in the heavens is hidden from Allah

3:6.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِ كَيۡفَ يَشَآءُۚ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
