62:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ لَفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
62:2.en: He it is Who hath sent among the unlettered ones a messenger of their own, to recite unto them His revelations and to make them grow, and to teach them the Scripture and wisdom, though heretofore they were indeed in error manifest

75:22.en: That day will faces be resplendent

39:67.ar: وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدۡرِهِۦ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ جَمِيعࣰ ا قَبۡضَتُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ مَطۡوِيَّٰتُۢ بِيَمِينِهِۦۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
39:67.en: And they esteem not Allah as He hath the right to be esteemed, when the whole earth is His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens are rolled in His right hand. Glorified is He and High Exalted from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)

2:255.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُۚ لَا تَأۡخُذُهُۥ سِنَةࣱ وَلَا نَوۡمࣱۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَشۡفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِهِۦۚ يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيۡءࣲ مِّنۡ عِلۡمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَۚ وَسِعَ كُرۡسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفۡظُهُمَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
2:255.en: Allah! There is no deity save Him, the Alive, the Eternal. Neither slumber nor sleep overtaketh Him. Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth. Who is he that intercedeth with Him save by His leave? He knoweth that which is in front of them and that which is behind them, while they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He will. His throne includeth the heavens and the earth, and He is never weary of preserving them. He is the Sublime, the Tremendous

hAcB3sEpOOs.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Final Episode
hAcB3sEpOOs.one_line: Why study Allah's names: knowing Him is the purpose of life, the root of love and obedience, and the source of freedom from people.
hAcB3sEpOOs.summary: Closing the series, he explains why the names matter. Speaking about Allah is the heaviest of subjects, and the Quran follows the image of a mountain humbled by revelation with a list of His names. Since Allah is outside time and space and cannot be imagined, His names are how we come to know Him, and knowing Him is the purpose of creation and the mark of the highest scholars. He shows how ignorance of particular names lies behind particular failings: stinginess, eating the unlawful, cheating, hatred, self-abasement before people, crippling fear and hopelessness. You cannot love someone you do not know, and ihsan, worshipping as if you see Him, is reached by knowing Him so well that only the seeing remains, which the people of Paradise will finally receive. Knowing the One who commands makes His commands easy and makes any sin serious, because what matters is whom you disobey. He urges people to make every transaction with Allah rather than with people, who are fickle, forgetful and as lost as anyone, so that service continues whether or not anyone is grateful. Everything else is leaving; Allah alone remains, and knowing Him brings a serenity and freedom no enemy can take away.

outline.heading: Opening
Why study the names in categories
outline.gist: Grouping names by meaning helps non-Arabic speakers call on Allah with the right names for each need.

outline.heading: The weight of speaking about Allah
outline.gist: No subject carries higher stakes; the Quran pictures a mountain humbled by revelation and then lists His names.

outline.heading: From names to attributes to knowing Him
outline.gist: Creation lets you appreciate His names, the names reveal His attributes, and the attributes lead you to know Him.

outline.heading: The highest people are those who know their Lord
outline.gist: Across every school, the greatest scholars are described as knowers of Allah, the ultimate goal of all knowledge.

outline.heading: Created to worship, meaning to know Him
outline.gist: The verse on the purpose of creating jinn and humans was explained as 'so that they may know Me'.

outline.heading: How can He be veiled when He made everything apparent
outline.gist: A classical meditation: He is manifest in, before and closer than everything, so nothing can truly veil Him.

outline.heading: He cannot be imagined, so we know Him through His names
outline.gist: We can picture the Prophet because he exists in time and space, but Allah created time and space and is known only through His names.

outline.heading: Each failing comes from not knowing a name
outline.gist: Stinginess, eating the unlawful, cheating, hatred, self-abasement, crippling fear and hopelessness each reflect ignorance of a specific name.

outline.heading: A name for every moment: call on Him by them
outline.gist: Every situation exposes you to one of His names; to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call Him by them.

outline.heading: You cannot love whom you do not know
outline.gist: The more you know Allah the more you love Him.

outline.heading: Ihsan: so close that only seeing remains
outline.gist: Worship as if you see Him by knowing His names until nothing is left but the actual seeing.

outline.heading: Every moment not knowing Him is wasted
outline.gist: Life is the opportunity to know God; prophets were sent to make Him known, since obedience makes no sense otherwise.

outline.heading: Seeing Allah in Paradise
outline.gist: Believers will see Him as clearly as the full moon, and when the veil is lifted nothing they were given is more beloved to them.

outline.heading: Lowest and highest in Paradise
outline.gist: The lowest rules a dominion many times the earth; the highest see His face morning and evening and simply wait for the next time.

outline.heading: Faces radiant, looking at their Lord
outline.gist: That seeing comes later; in this life worship as if you see Him, which requires knowing Him first.

outline.heading: Know Allah through how He describes Himself
outline.gist: No words suffice but His own, so read the Quran; people did not revere Allah as He deserves, though the earth will be in His grip.

outline.heading: Ayat al-Kursi and al-Ikhlas are pure description
outline.gist: The greatest verse and the surah equal to a third of the Quran simply describe Allah.

outline.heading: Joy in His name
outline.gist: Knowing Him makes mentioning and hearing His name a joy; He is with the servant whose lips move in His remembrance.

outline.heading: Know the commander and the commands become easy
outline.gist: What matters is who gave the command, not the command itself.

outline.heading: Sin is about whom you disobey
outline.gist: Those who know Allah find any sin unthinkable, because the issue is not its size but that it disobeys the Almighty.

outline.heading: Your transaction is with Allah, not people
outline.gist: People's moods and loyalties change and will let you down; Allah's treatment of you never changes, so deal with Him.

outline.heading: Giving and receiving charity through Allah
outline.gist: The giver gives to Allah through the needy and the receiver takes his provision from Allah through the giver; serve people regardless of their gratitude while taking feedback.

outline.heading: Live through the names
outline.gist: In need, fear, worry or poverty, connect to the matching name; this is the greatest investment of a life.

outline.heading: Everything is leaving; only Allah remains
outline.gist: We live a few laps around the sun with a unique chance to know Him, which brings unmatched serenity.

outline.heading: My paradise is in my chest
outline.gist: Prison becomes seclusion, exile becomes travel and death becomes martyrdom; knowing Allah gives a liberty no enemy can touch.

outline.heading: Everyone is as lost as you: care only for His opinion
outline.gist: People are clinging to a raft; only Allah's view of you matters, and whoever finds Him lacks nothing while whoever misses Him finds nothing.

outline.heading: Outro
